subject.title: fix(openai): allow RFC 2544 fake-IP range for Realtime session requests

question: Should OpenAI Realtime session-secret requests get a hostname-scoped fake-IP SSRF exception for `api.openai.com`, and should that reuse a newly public Plugin SDK helper or stay as a local policy literal?
rationale: The code shape is narrow and supported by proof, but accepting an SSRF exception and expanding Plugin SDK API surface are maintainer security/API policy choices rather than routine contributor follow-up.

options.title: Accept Scoped Exception After Rebase
options.body: Accept the host-scoped fake-IP policy for OpenAI Realtime, then require the contributor to rebase, refresh SDK budgets, and rerun the focused API/test checks before merge.

options.title: Keep The Policy Local
options.body: Use the same narrow policy as an OpenAI-local `SsrFPolicy` literal and avoid adding a new public `plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` export.

options.title: Decline Realtime Fake-IP Relaxation
options.body: Keep proxy DNS exclusions or disabling fake-IP mode as the supported workaround for Realtime if maintainers do not want this SSRF exception.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Exception After Rebase
recommendation.body: Accept the host-scoped fake-IP policy for OpenAI Realtime, then require the contributor to rebase, refresh SDK budgets, and rerun the focused API/test checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the fake-IP SSRF helper and appears in current history for the Realtime/SSRF surfaces this decision affects.
